ownership_summary: GCC operations are branches of Citibank, N.A. and affiliates of Citigroup Inc. (US). The GCC entities are not separately listed; Citigroup ownership not recorded for this GCC profile.
group_structure: Citi runs its GCC business as part of the Middle East and Africa (MEA) cluster within its International franchise. In the UAE: Citibank N.A. UAE Branch (CBUAE; consumer, Citigold, Citigold Private Client, cards, plus institutional), Citibank N.A. DIFC (DFSA: deposits, credit, advising and arranging - used for private banking/institutional), Citigroup Global Markets Limited DIFC Branch (advising/arranging), and an ADGM branch (liquidity management). Citi Private Bank serves Middle East clients from a Dubai office under the Head of UK, Europe & Middle East. Saudi Arabia: regional headquarters for MENA opened in Riyadh (Kingdom Tower) in Oct 2025. Bahrain: consumer business sold to Ahli United Bank (closed 1 Dec 2022); institutional business retained. In April 2021 Citi named the UAE one of four Asia/EMEA consumer wealth centres (with Singapore, Hong Kong, London) while exiting consumer banking in 13 markets incl. Bahrain. Group figures below are Citigroup (global); no UAE or GCC financial statements were found.

capabilities.wealth_summary: Citi kept the UAE as one of four Asia/EMEA consumer wealth centres in its 2021 strategy (with Singapore, Hong Kong and London) while exiting consumer banking in 13 markets, including Bahrain, whose consumer business was sold to Ahli United Bank in Dec 2022. In the UAE it runs Citigold (USD 200k) and Citigold Private Client (USD 1m, with onshore/offshore UAE-Singapore booking managed by one UAE-based RM), plus Citi Private Bank from a Dubai office. Rajeev Garg became Head of Wealth for Citibank UAE on 18 Jun 2026, reporting to Asia South Wealth. The UAE shelf includes mutual funds (buy/sell in Citi Mobile), bonds, structured notes, e-brokerage in US (and per another page UK, French and German) equities and bonds, FX Order Watch, securities-backed finance, and a Citi Model Portfolio reference tool with five risk-based allocations revised quarterly. Citibank N.A. UAE holds SCA licences for advice, international brokerage, portfolio management and custody. No UAE or GCC wealth figures are disclosed; global Wealth client balances were USD 1.35trn at 30 Jun 2026.

initiatives.what: Appointed Rajeev Garg Head of Wealth, Citibank UAE (Citigold, Citigold Private Client, cards), with a mandate to upgrade risk and control processes.
Named Karim Tannir MEA Cluster and Banking Head (Dubai) effective August; Ebru Pakcan moves to COO, International and Legacy Franchises.
Opened MENA regional headquarters in Kingdom Tower, Riyadh (licence received 2024).
Named 25-year veteran Carmen Haddad vice chair for Middle East private banking (Bloomberg, search result only).
Completed sale of Bahrain consumer business (retail, cards, unsecured lending; ~175 staff) to Ahli United Bank; institutional business retained.
Strategy refresh: Asia/EMEA consumer focused on four wealth centres incl. the UAE; exits from consumer franchises in 13 markets incl. Bahrain.

opportunities: UAE is one of Citi's four Asia/EMEA consumer wealth centres (S5), with a new UAE Head of Wealth since Jun 2026 (S15).
Model portfolios are a reference tool only, and no discretionary service is described despite an SCA portfolio management licence (S11, S6).
Self-directed trading limited to US (possibly UK/France/Germany) equities and bonds; no UAE/GCC markets or ETFs confirmed (S10, S9).
No Shariah or private-markets products on UAE pages (S9).
barriers: UAE wealth reports into Citi's Asia South Wealth line; platforms and house views (Citi Mobile, model portfolios) are group-run (S15, S11).
Small UAE retail footprint: 4 branches and 3 Citigold lounges (S6).
New UAE wealth head's stated mandate prioritises risk and control upgrades (S15).
